skill.name: azure-keyvault-secrets-ts
skill.description: Reference examples for using Azure Key Vault Secrets and Keys SDKs in Node.js TypeScript applications.
skill.summary: Use Azure Key Vault SDK patterns to create, retrieve, rotate, and manage secrets and keys in TypeScript.

security_audit.summary: The static shell, environment, network, and sensitive-file findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, TypeScript examples, and normal Azure SDK configuration. Semantic review found real documentation risks: one example logs a secret value, and purge operations are shown without sufficient safeguards.

remediation.suggestion: Remove console output of secret values and show masked handling or passing the value directly to a secure consumer.
Add warnings, RBAC prerequisites, confirmation steps, and recovery expectations before purgeDeletedSecret and purgeDeletedKey examples.

remediation.issue: Documentation mixes secrets, keys, and cryptographic examples under a secrets-only skill name.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify scope and required packages for key and cryptography examples so users do not apply incomplete guidance.

content.user_title: Manage Azure Key Vault Secrets in TypeScript
content.value_statement: Secret handling in TypeScript services is easy to implement incorrectly. This skill provides Azure Key Vault SDK patterns for retrieval, rotation, deletion, backup, and recovery.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install Azure Key Vault Secrets and Azure Identity packages.
Demonstrates DefaultAzureCredential with a vault URL from environment configuration.
Provides examples for creating, reading, listing, deleting, purging, and recovering secrets.
Includes Azure Key Vault key creation, rotation, deletion, and property listing examples.
Shows cryptography client examples for encryption, decryption, signing, verification, and key wrapping.
Covers backup and restore flows for keys and secrets.
limitations: The skill is documentation only and does not execute Azure SDK calls for the user.
Examples require valid Azure credentials, vault permissions, and installed SDK packages.
Some examples include keys and cryptography APIs beyond the secrets package named in the skill.
The sample should be revised before production use because it logs a secret value.

use_cases.title: Add Secret Retrieval to a Service
use_cases.description: Use the examples to wire DefaultAzureCredential and SecretClient into a Node.js service.

use_cases.title: Plan Key Rotation Workflows
use_cases.description: Review rotation policy and key operation examples before implementing Azure Key Vault governance.

use_cases.title: Document Recovery Procedures
use_cases.description: Use delete, recover, backup, and restore examples to draft operational runbooks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Secret Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a Node.js TypeScript application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to configure an Azure Key Vault SecretClient in TypeScript using DefaultAzureCredential and an environment-provided vault name.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve Secrets Safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Application secret loading without logging sensitive values.
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the Azure Key Vault secret retrieval example so it avoids printing secret values and validates missing secrets cleanly.

prompt_templates.title: Design Rotation and Deletion Flows
prompt_templates.scenario: Production lifecycle planning for keys and secrets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a TypeScript workflow for rotating Key Vault keys, setting expiration dates, and handling soft delete recovery.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Key Vault Integration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced security review of an existing implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my TypeScript Azure Key Vault integration for unsafe secret logging, overbroad key operations, missing RBAC checks, and risky purge behavior.

output_examples.input: I need to connect a TypeScript service to Azure Key Vault.
output_examples.output: A concise setup plan with required packages, credential choice, vault URL configuration, and a safe client initialization pattern.

output_examples.input: I want to fetch a secret without exposing it.
output_examples.output: Guidance that retrieves the secret for internal use, avoids console logging, handles missing values, and recommends least-privilege access.

output_examples.input: I need an operations guide for deleting a Key Vault secret.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step runbook covering soft delete, recovery, purge approval, permissions, and audit logging requirements.

best_practices: Use managed identity or DefaultAzureCredential instead of hardcoded credentials.
Mask or avoid displaying secret values in logs, terminals, and AI transcripts.
Grant only the Key Vault permissions required for each application workflow.
anti_patterns: Printing secret values after retrieval for debugging or demonstrations.
Granting purge permissions to application identities that only need read access.
Using sample secret names and values unchanged in production code.

faq.question: Does this skill run Azure commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides TypeScript SDK examples that users can adapt in their own projects.

faq.question: Which Azure authentication method does it show?
faq.answer: It shows DefaultAzureCredential from the Azure Identity SDK.

faq.question: Can it manage both secrets and keys?
faq.answer: Yes. The document includes SecretClient, KeyClient, and CryptographyClient examples.

faq.question: Is it safe to log retrieved secret values?
faq.answer: No. Secret values should be masked or passed directly to secure consumers.

faq.question: Does browser JavaScript support these SDK examples?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that these SDKs are Node.js only.

faq.question: What permissions are required?
faq.answer: Permissions depend on the operation. Read, write, delete, purge, backup, and restore should be granted separately.
